gloss: move, prompt (of the heart); offer freely, volunteer; freewill offering; willing, noble
summary: נָדַב is what a man's own heart does when it moves him to give: Israel brought the tabernacle's materials, “every man whose heart moved him” (Exo 25:2; 35:21, 29), and in the hithpael men offer themselves for war or service, or give freely to Yahweh's house (Jdg 5:2, 9; 1Ch 29:9, 17). נְדָבָה is what is so given, above all the freewill offering, which no command or vow requires and which stands beside the vows and the appointed offerings of the feasts (Lev 22:23; 23:38). נָדִיב is the one whose heart is willing (Exo 35:5), and so the open-handed man of rank, the noble, set beside princes and kings and against the fool (Num 21:18; Isa 32:5, 8). Arabic nadaba “call, urge someone to a thing” and intadaba “answer the call, hasten to it” show the same impulse to act.

words.gloss: willing, moved to give; noble, a noble; noble-minded
words.summary: First the one whose heart is willing to give (Exo 35:5, 22); then, mostly in poetry and wisdom, a noble, a man of rank beside princes and kings; and in Isaiah and Proverbs one noble in conduct, set against the fool. Pro 19:6 sets the נָדִיב beside “the man of gifts”, which joins the generous and the great man. No cognate found shares the sense “noble” by itself; it rests on the text, where the noble is the giving man, and on the root’s “willing, given freely” (the Targum of Isaiah even renders נְדִיבִים at Isa 13:2 with מְנַדְּבִין, “givers”).

senses.definition: Of a person, and of the heart or spirit, ready of one's own accord to give or to serve; mostly in the phrase נְדִיב לֵב, “willing of heart”.

evidence.note: “Take from among you a contribution for Yahweh: כֹּל נְדִיב לִבּוֹ, let him bring it”: the gift is from whoever is willing.
Men and women came, כֹּל נְדִיב לֵב, and brought their gold; the same people of whom 35:21 says their spirit moved them (נָדְבָה).
The assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, “and every נְדִיב לֵב burnt offerings”: the burnt offerings came from those who were willing.
With Solomon in all the work will be “every נָדִיב with wisdom for any service”: the willing who are skilled.
“Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and uphold me with a רוּחַ נְדִיבָה”: a willing spirit, parallel to the joy restored.

senses.definition: A man of high standing among the people: a noble or prince, named beside שָׂרִים, kings and rulers, and over against the poor.

evidence.note: “A well the שָׂרִים dug, the נְדִיבֵי of the people delved”: parallel to princes.
“By me שָׂרִים rule, וּנְדִיבִים, all the judges of righteousness.”
Does one say to a מֶלֶךְ “Worthless!”, to נְדִיבִים “Wicked!”?: parallel to king.
Yahweh raises the poor from the dust “to seat them with נְדִיבִים, and he gives them a throne of glory to inherit”.
“To seat him with נְדִיבִים, with the נְדִיבֵי of his people”: Hannah's words again (Psa 113:7–8).
Their נְדִיבִים like Oreb and Zeeb, parallel to “all their נְסִיכִים”, the princes of Midian.
“The נְדִיבֵי of the peoples are gathered, the people of the God of Abraham.”
“He pours contempt on נְדִיבִים” (also Job 12:21).
“Better to take refuge in Yahweh than to trust in נְדִיבִים.”
“Do not trust in נְדִיבִים, in a son of man in whom there is no salvation”: the noble is only a man.
Better to be told “Come up here” than to be put lower before a נָדִיב.
It is not good to strike נְדִיבִים for uprightness.
The armies called against Babylon “enter the gates of the נְדִיבִים”.
“Where is the house of the נָדִיב, and where the tent of the wicked?”: the great man fallen; here one who used his rank for evil.
The bride is “daughter of a נָדִיב”.
מַרְכְּבוֹת עַמִּי־נָדִיב, “the chariots of my noble people”: the same two words as the name עַמִּינָדָב.

senses.definition: Noble in what one plans and does: open-handed and honourable, not by birth but by conduct; the feminine plural נְדִיבוֹת is “noble things”.

evidence.note: “The fool (נָבָל) will no longer be called נָדִיב, nor the scoundrel (כִּילַי) said to be noble”: the name will fit the man.
“But the נָדִיב plans נְדִיבוֹת, and by נְדִיבוֹת he stands”: nobility shown in counsel and deed.
Fine speech does not suit a נָבָל, “how much less lying lips a נָדִיב”.
“Many entreat the favour of a נָדִיב, and everyone is a friend to the אִישׁ מַתָּן”: the noble is the man who gives.

evidence.locator: Psa.146.3, נְדִיבִים → ἄρχοντας; Psa.113.8, Psa.118.9, Job.12.21, Isa.13.2 the same; ἄρχων renders נָדִיב ×10

evidence.note: “None of the ἀρχόντων of this age knew” the wisdom of God: the rulers in whom Psa 146:3 forbids trust.

evidence.locator: 1Sa.2.8, נְדִיבִים → δυναστῶν; Pro.17.26, Pro.25.7 the same

evidence.note: Mary takes up Hannah's song (1Sa 2:7–8): “He has put down δυνάστας from thrones and exalted the lowly.”
“The spirit is πρόθυμον, but the flesh is weak” (Mar 14:38): the willing spirit, as רוּחַ נְדִיבָה in Psa 51:14; not a quotation.
“So, as much as is in me, I am πρόθυμον to preach the gospel to you.”

parallels.note: Prince, official, beside it of men of rank.
King, beside it as men no one dares rebuke.
Prince, beside it of Midian's leaders.
Son of man: what a noble is, and why he cannot save.
The man of gifts, beside the noble.

opposites.note: The fool, who will no longer be called noble.
The scoundrel, the grasping man, set against the noble.
The poor man raised from the dust to sit with nobles; with אֶבְיוֹן, the needy.

words.gloss: freewill offering, free gift; willingness, freely
words.summary: What is given because the giver's heart moves him: in the law, an offering no command or vow requires, named with the vows and kept apart from them; in the building of the tabernacle and the second house, gifts of materials and silver and gold; and, as an adverb, “freely”, of Yahweh's love (Hos 14:5).

senses.definition: A burnt offering or peace offering brought of the offerer's own will, not owed by a command or by a vow; the law names it beside the vow (נֶדֶר) and beside the offerings appointed for the feasts, and treats it more leniently than a vow.

evidence.note: After the appointed times of Lev 23: their offerings are “besides the sabbaths of Yahweh, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your נִדְבוֹת which you give to Yahweh”.
“These you shall do to Yahweh at your appointed times, besides your vows and your נְדָבוֹת”: the freewill offering is over and above what the feasts require.
An ox or lamb with a limb too long or too short “you may make a נְדָבָה, but for a vow it will not be accepted”: distinguished from the vow.
“If the sacrifice of his offering is a vow or a נְדָבָה”, it may be eaten that day and the next: a peace offering.
“For any of their vows or any of their נְדָבוֹת which they offer to Yahweh as a burnt offering.”
A peace offering “to fulfil a vow or as a נְדָבָה” must be whole, without blemish.
A burnt offering or sacrifice “to fulfil a vow, or as a נְדָבָה, or at your appointed times”.
To be brought to the place Yahweh chooses, with vows, tithes and firstborn (also Deu 12:17).
“As you vowed to Yahweh your God a נְדָבָה, which you spoke with your mouth”: freely promised, but once spoken it must be kept.
The feast of שָׁבֻעוֹת is kept “with the tribute of a נִדְבַת יָדְךָ, which you shall give as Yahweh your God blesses you”: its measure set by the giver, according to Yahweh's blessing.
When the prince in Ezekiel's house makes a נְדָבָה, the east gate is opened for him.
“Proclaim נְדָבוֹת, make them heard”: Israel's showy freewill offerings, mocked.
“With a נְדָבָה I will sacrifice to you; I will praise your name, Yahweh.”
After the continual offering, the new moons and the appointed times, the offerings of “everyone who offered freely a נְדָבָה to Yahweh”.
Kore was over “the נִדְבוֹת of God”.
Josiah's princes gave לִנְדָבָה, freely, to the people, priests and Levites for the Passover.

senses.gloss: free gift (of materials, silver and gold)
senses.definition: Goods given freely for Yahweh's house: the materials for the tabernacle, and the silver and gold sent with the returning exiles.

evidence.note: “Every man and woman whose heart moved them (נָדַב לִבָּם) to bring … the sons of Israel brought a נְדָבָה to Yahweh”: the verb and the noun together.
“And they still brought him נְדָבָה morning by morning”, until there was more than enough (36:5–7).
The exiles are to be given silver, gold and goods “with the נְדָבָה for the house of God which is in Jerusalem”.
“The silver and the gold are a נְדָבָה to Yahweh the God of your fathers.”

senses.gloss: freely, of free will; abundance freely given
senses.definition: Used of the manner of giving rather than the gift: freely, unprompted by anything outside the giver; of Yahweh's love and rain, of the praise of a man's mouth, and of the Messiah's people.

evidence.note: “I will heal their turning away, I will love them נְדָבָה, for my anger has turned from him”: Yahweh's love given freely.
“A rain of נְדָבוֹת you shed abroad, God; your inheritance, when it was weary, you established it”: rain given freely and in plenty.
“Your people are נְדָבֹת in the day of your power”: the people of the king at Yahweh's right hand (110:1) are themselves freewill offerings, willing.
“Accept, Yahweh, the נִדְבוֹת of my mouth”: praise offered as a freewill offering.

evidence.locator: Lev.7.16, נְדָבָה → ἑκούσιον; Num.15.3, Ezr.3.5, Psa.68.10 the same; Ezr.1.4 ἑκουσίου; Ezr.8.28 ἑκούσια

evidence.note: Paul would do nothing without Philemon's consent, “that your good might not be as of necessity but κατὰ ἑκούσιον”: of free will, the freewill offering's own quality.
Shepherd the flock “not by compulsion but ἑκουσίως”.

greek.gloss: confession; (of a gift) what is avowed

evidence.locator: Ezk.46.12, נְדָבָה → ὁμολογίαν; Amo.4.5 ὁμολογίας; Hos.14.5 ὁμολόγως

evidence.note: Of the Corinthians' gift for the saints: they glorify God “for the obedience of your ὁμολογίας to the gospel … and the liberality of your contribution”.
“Not that I seek the δόμα, but I seek the fruit that abounds to your account”: the Philippians' gift, “a sweet-smelling savour, a sacrifice acceptable” (4:18).

parallels.note: The vow: named with the freewill offering again and again, and distinguished from it (Lev 22:23).
Gifts, listed beside the freewill offerings after the feasts.
The contribution lifted off for Yahweh, which the willing brought as נְדָבָה.

phrases.gloss: a vow or a freewill offering
the freewill offering of your hand
the freewill offerings of my mouth: praise

words.gloss: move, prompt (to give); (hithpael) offer freely, volunteer

stems.gloss: move, prompt (of the heart or spirit)

senses.definition: Always with the heart or spirit as subject and the person as object: a man's own heart moves him to give. Used only of the gifts for the tabernacle.

evidence.note: “From every man אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ, you shall take my contribution”: whose heart moves him.
“Everyone whose heart lifted him (נְשָׂאוֹ לִבּוֹ), and everyone whom his spirit moved (נָדְבָה רוּחוֹ אֹתוֹ)”: parallel to the lifted heart.
“Every man and woman whose heart moved them (נָדַב לִבָּם אֹתָם) to bring”, and what they brought is called נְדָבָה.

senses.gloss: offer oneself, volunteer (for war or service)
senses.definition: To give oneself of one's own will: to come forward for battle, for a post, or to live in Jerusalem.

evidence.note: “When leaders led in Israel, בְּהִתְנַדֵּב עָם, when the people offered themselves, bless Yahweh”: the tribes coming to fight under Deborah and Barak.
“My heart is toward the commanders of Israel, הַמִּתְנַדְּבִים among the people.”
Amasiah son of Zichri, “who offered himself willingly to Yahweh”, with 200,000 mighty men.
“The people blessed all the men הַמִּתְנַדְּבִים to dwell in Jerusalem”: beside those chosen by lot (11:1).

senses.gloss: give freely, make a freewill offering
senses.definition: To give gifts or offerings of one's own will, for Yahweh's house or altar.

evidence.note: “The people rejoiced because they had offered freely, for with a whole heart they offered freely to Yahweh.”
“You test the heart and are pleased with uprightness; in the uprightness of my heart I have offered freely all these, and now I have seen your people … offer freely to you with joy.”
“Who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to offer freely like this? For all things come from you, and of your own hand we have given you.”
“Who is offering freely to fill his hand today for Yahweh?”
Then the heads of the fathers and the princes offered freely.
Gifts for the returning exiles, “besides all that was freely offered”.
Heads of fathers “offered freely for the house of God, to set it up in its place”.
“Everyone who offered freely a נְדָבָה to Yahweh”: the verb with its noun.
The verb is not in the New Testament; its noun is: “If the προθυμία is there first, it is accepted according to what one has”, of the gift for the saints, as David's people gave.

evidence.locator: Jdg.5.9, הַמִּתְנַדְּבִים → ἑκουσιαζόμενοι; Ezr.2.68, Ezr.3.5, Neh.11.2 the same verb

evidence.note: Not in the New Testament; its adjective ἑκούσιος is, “of free will” (see נְדָבָה).

parallels.note: “His heart lifted him”, beside “his spirit moved him”.

phrases.gloss: they offered freely with a whole heart

words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic, only in Artaxerxes' letter to Ezra, with the same two uses as the Hebrew hithpael: to offer oneself to go up to Jerusalem, and to give silver and gold for the house of God.

senses.definition: To be willing of oneself to go.

evidence.note: “Everyone in my kingdom of the people of Israel … כָל־מִתְנַדַּב to go to Jerusalem, let him go with you.”

senses.definition: To give freely for the house of God.

evidence.note: “The silver and gold which the king and his counsellors הִתְנַדַּבוּ to the God of Israel.”
“The priests מִתְנַדְּבִין for the house of their God.”

words.summary: An Aramaic verbal noun of the hithpaal, once (Ezr 7:16), answering to Hebrew נְדָבָה. The database files its one token under the verb's key, so it has no key of its own here.

senses.definition: What the people and priests gave freely for the house of God.

evidence.note: “With הִתְנַדָּבוּת עַמָּא, the freewill offering of the people, and the priests giving freely.”

words.summary: Once (Job 30:15), with a suffix: Job's standing as a noble, the honour of the נָדִיב he had been (Job 29:7–25). One use, so the sense rests on the context and on נָדִיב. No cognate has been found for it; it is tied to the root through נָדִיב.

senses.definition: The standing and honour of a noble.

evidence.note: “Terrors are turned on me; they pursue נְדִבָתִי like the wind, and my welfare has passed like a cloud”: parallel to יְשֻׁעָתִי, his welfare.

cognates.gloss: call, summon, invite someone to a thing; urge, incite him to it; send him to do it
cognates.note: Lane's sources give “he called, summoned, or invited him to the thing … and instigated, incited, or urged him to it”, to war or to help, and “nothing incited me (mā nadabanī) to what I did but sincerity towards you”: an inner motive prompting a deed, as a man's heart prompts him in Exo 25:2. Its noun nudba is “a call, a summons”, and mandūb “one sent to do a thing”.

cognates.gloss: answer a call, comply; hasten to someone, when called to war or to help, or of one's own accord
cognates.note: Form VIII, the reflexive of nadaba: “he answered, or complied with … his call … and hastened to him, when called to war, succour, &c.”, and “they hastened to him, either at his call, or of their own accord”. This is the Hebrew hithpael's offering oneself for war (Jdg 5:2, 9), with the same reflexive sense in a t-stem.

cognates.gloss: a man quick and ready in carrying out an affair; clever, excellent
cognates.note: “A man who, when he is sent to accomplish a great … affair, finds it light to him: clever … excellent”; the verb nadub “he was light, active … excellent”. A man of ready and excellent action is near the Hebrew נָדִיב, the willing and noble; but the Arabic stresses quickness and capability, not generosity or rank, so it is recorded as possible.

Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the pael and ithpaal “to donate; to be devoted to”; the Targum of Isaiah renders נְדִיבִים (Isa 13:2) with the participle מְנַדְּבִין, and the Targum of Psalms uses the root at Psa 110:3; “Israelites will grow rich and offer donations” (Pes. 50a). The same giving freely as the Hebrew hithpael and נְדָבָה.

evidence.note: “Pa. נַדֵּב, Ithpa. אִתְנַדֵּב … to donate; to be devoted to. Targ. Is. XIII, 2 מְנַדְּבִין … Targ. Ps. CX, 3. Pes. 50ᵃ … ומִתְנַדְּבֵי Israelites will … offer donations.”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh asked for the tabernacle's materials only from those whose own heart moved them (Exo 25:2; 35:5, 21–22, 29), and the law kept a place, beside the vows and the appointed offerings of the feasts, for the freewill offering that nothing required (Lev 23:38; Num 29:39). David's people rejoiced that they gave “with a whole heart”, and David confessed that even so they gave Yahweh only what was his: “all things come from you, and of your own hand we have given you”; he knew that Yahweh tests the heart (1Ch 29:9, 14, 17). Paul asks the same of the gift for the saints: it is accepted by the willingness behind it, according to what a man has, and each is to give “as he has purposed in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loves a cheerful giver” (2Co 8:12; 9:7). What God looks for in a gift is the heart that moves it.

Hannah says that Yahweh raises the poor from the dust to sit with נְדִיבִים and inherit a throne of glory, and Psalm 113 repeats it; Mary takes it up when she says God has put down rulers from their thrones and exalted the lowly (1Sa 2:8; Psa 113:7–8; Luk 1:52). Isaiah says that when a king reigns in righteousness the fool will no longer be called נָדִיב, and the noble will be the one who plans and stands by noble things (Isa 32:1, 5, 8). So in the kingdom nobility is what God gives to the lowly he raises, and what a man's conduct shows, not what men's rank confers; and trust is not to be put in nobles, who are only men (Psa 146:3).

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Lev 23:38 (נִדְבוֹתֵיכֶם) and Num 10:14 (עַמִּינָדָב). Root key נדב as the database has it. Left out: נִדְבָּךְ (xn.ac.ab, Ezr 6:4 ×2, “course, layer” of stone or timber), which the database files under this root but which is the Akkadian nadbāku/natbāku “layer, course of bricks” (Oracc akk natbāku, norms nadbāku, nadabāku), a noun of tabāku “pour out, heap up”, borrowed into Aramaic; it is not formed from נדב. Akkadian nindabû “(food) offering” (Oracc, also spelled nidbû) looks like נְדָבָה but is the Sumerian nindaba (attested from Early Dynastic), so it is not recorded as a cognate. Arabic ندب also has senses with no evident tie to the Hebrew: “bewail the dead, enumerating his virtues” (nadaba al-mayyita), “scar” (nadab) and “wager” (Lane pp. 2778–2779); ב and ד are not merged letters, so they cannot show a split; left unrecorded. Aramaic הִתְנַדָּבוּת (Ezr 7:16) has no BDB key of its own: its token is counted under xn.ac.aa with the verb. Proper names left for name entries: נָדָב Nadab (n.bc.ab: Aaron's son, Jeroboam's son, a Jerahmeelite, a Gibeonite), נְדַבְיָה Nedabiah (n.bc.ag), אֲבִינָדָב Abinadab (a.ae.aq), אֲחִינָדָב Ahinadab (a.ck.as), יְהוֹנָדָב/יוֹנָדָב Jehonadab (e.az.aq/bq), and מַכְנַדְבַי Machnadebai (m.bx.aj), which BDB files under other roots; נוֹדָב Nodab (n.bc.af, 1Ch 5:19) is a people the eastern tribes fought beside the Hagrites, Jetur and Naphish, not a person, and has no tokens under its key. No Syriac ndb is in the Peshitta New Testament (SEDRA). Not followed: Old South Arabian and Ugaritic ndb, not in the vendored sources.
